input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants only for-cause, insolvency, and security/service-level termination rights (9.1-9.3); there is no Section 9.4 and no convenience right anywhere (the only hit for "convenience" is the purchase-order definition in 1.6). The term is three years (8.1) and Section 2.1 expressly locks Customer into a take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under this rule, so it fails both the preferred and fallback positions. We inserted a new Section 9.4 at the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right), expressly overriding Section 2.1; Vendor has no convenience right today, so no deletion is needed there.

ops.text: Notwithstanding Section 2.1, Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without early-termination fee or other penalty, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since the three-year take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 currently leaves us with no exit. If a longer runway helps, we can move to 60 days' notice.
proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, overriding Section 2.1's no-termination language.
